title: On the Incarnation in 9 days
about: St Athanasius' classic, a few chapters a day.

items.text: St Athanasius wrote this short book as a young man, around 318. It is one of the clearest books ever written on why God became man. Read the chapters named for each day.
Why begin with creation? Because the One who made us is the One who saves us.

items.father: St Athanasius, On the Incarnation, chapters 1–5

items.text: God's 'dilemma': man was perishing, and it was not fitting that God's work should be undone.

items.father: St Athanasius, On the Incarnation, chapters 6–10

items.text: Men forgot God, so the Word came to renew the knowledge of Him.

items.father: St Athanasius, On the Incarnation, chapters 11–16

items.text: The Word in the body, yet not confined by it.

items.father: St Athanasius, On the Incarnation, chapters 17–21

items.text: Why the Cross, and why in public?

items.father: St Athanasius, On the Incarnation, chapters 22–26

items.text: The Resurrection, and the proof of it: Christians no longer fear death.

items.father: St Athanasius, On the Incarnation, chapters 27–32

items.text: Answers to the Jews, from the Prophets.

items.father: St Athanasius, On the Incarnation, chapters 33–40
St Athanasius, On the Incarnation, chapters 41–48

items.text: 'He became man that we might become god.' And how to read the Scriptures: with a pure life.

items.father: St Athanasius, On the Incarnation, chapters 49–57
